newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: World refined copper consumption down in July.
newsitem.headline: World refined copper consumption down in July.

text.p: World refined copper consumption was down by six percent and refined production remained at about the same rate in July compared with June, the International Copper Study Group (ICSG) said.

Consumption was 1.4 percent higher and mine and refined production were eight percent and 6.7 percent higher respectively in the first seven months of 1996, compared with the same year-ago period, the ICSG said in a statement.
Refined stocks on the LME were 243,000 tonnes at the end of July, markedly lower than the 366,000 tonnes reported at the end of January 1996, the ICSG said.
The average LME spot price for June 1996 was $2,170 per metric tonne, while for July and August it was lower at $1,984 and $2,008 per tonne respectively.
World refined copper consumption and supply trends, 1995-96
(1) = Refined stocks include those held by exchanges, producers, consumers, merchants and governments in western economies.
(2) = Surplus or deficit is calculated using total refined production minus refined consumption.
